answer: Fresh wallets mint in a second; uncorrelated partners do not. A new identity may not vote or grade until its bond has collected nectar—settled fees—from seven counterparties whose funding graphs and signing keys share no ancestor. Each partner co-locks a slice of that bond, slashed with the principal if the newcomer is proven a replica. Applicants tracing to the same funder are bound as one beam of timber, joint weight capped at one seat. The fable that more keys mean more voice fails, because voice arrives only after uncorrelated trade has seasoned the stake, which is costly to fake in bulk.
